summary: Associated Press reports that Randal Quran Reid was arrested in Georgia on Louisiana warrants after facial-recognition technology linked him to a theft in a state he said he had never visited. His complaint alleged that the detective relied solely on the match, omitted basic location corroboration and did not disclose the technology in the warrant affidavit. Reid spent six days in jail before photographs and video supplied by his family and counsel led the sheriff's office to request withdrawal of the warrant. The later federal case settled for $200,000 without an admission of fault.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Exhaustive 74-class re-adjudication retains Inferential Evidence–Authority Separation and Required Verification Completion and admits Authorship and Source Attribution Integrity as an independent mechanism. The complaint-based Associated Press account reports that the warrant affidavit described the identification as coming from a credible source without disclosing the facial-recognition origin. That source-role substitution materially altered how the evidentiary basis was represented within a coercive warrant pathway.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The facial-recognition result supplied a candidate identity but did not independently establish probable cause or authority to detain Reid. The reported process nevertheless used the match as the operative identity basis for arrest warrants, converting uncertain biometric evidence into coercive public authority without adequate independent corroboration.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: AP reports the complaint's allegation that the detective did not conduct even a basic location search and the sheriff's-office reminder that a facial-recognition result required additional evidence or leads for an arrest warrant. Reid's location and visible physical differences were material falsification checks, yet the identification proceeded through the warrant process without them.

The warrant account reportedly characterised the identification as coming from a credible source without disclosing its facial-recognition origin, materially changing the represented source role of the identity evidence.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Associated Press reports that Randal Quran Reid was arrested in Georgia on Louisiana warrants after facial-recognition technology linked him to a theft in a state he said he had never visited. AP attributes to Reid's federal complaint allegations that the detective relied solely on the match, did not perform a basic location check and described the identification in the warrant affidavit as coming from a credible source without disclosing facial recognition. The report also states that Reid's family retained Louisiana counsel and supplied photographs and video showing that the surveillance subject was heavier and lacked Reid's mole; the sheriff's office then requested withdrawal of the warrant, and Reid was released after six days. Later reporting identifies Clearview AI as the tool and records a $200,000 settlement without an admission of fault.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence combines three evidence-governance failures. A facial-recognition similarity result that could validly operate as an investigative lead was reportedly promoted into the identity basis for warrants and detention without adequate independent corroboration. Material falsification checks—most notably location and physical-difference checks—were reportedly omitted before that identity was presented through the warrant process. Separately, the warrant account reportedly described the identification as coming from a credible source without disclosing the facial-recognition origin, changing the represented provenance of the evidence in a way material to interpretation and accountability. The classification remains bounded to the allegations preserved by the Associated Press account and does not convert the later settlement into an adjudication of fault.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows that inferential/authority separation and verification are complementary controls. CAM should require machine-generated identity candidates to remain explicitly provisional, disclose their origin to each consequential reviewer, and pass independent falsification checks before coercive action. Contestability must also be operational early enough that obvious disconfirming evidence can stop or reverse the action without requiring private counsel and days of detention.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Resolve the Associated Press account and its explicitly attributed complaint propositions into the distinction between biometric inference, required corroboration and coercive decision authority.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Reid's complaint alleged that the detective relied solely on a facial-recognition match to seek an arrest warrant.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A biometric similarity result remains evidence for an investigative lead; it does not independently establish identity, probable cause or authority for detention.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The reported process promoted an unresolved identity inference into the basis for warrants and coercive action without a separately established identity basis.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The complaint said a basic search would have shown Reid was in Georgia when the Louisiana theft occurred, and a reported sheriff's-office email reiterated that facial-recognition results require additional evidence or leads for an arrest warrant.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: When a consequential workflow requires corroboration, readily available checks capable of falsifying the candidate identity must be completed before the result is represented as warrant-ready.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The reported workflow omitted a required, materially falsifying location check and other independent evidence before presenting the identity through the warrant process.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The warrant affidavit referred to a credible source and still photographs but did not disclose the use of facial-recognition technology, according to Reid's complaint and counsel.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A consequential reviewer must know when an asserted identity originated as a machine-generated similarity lead so that the inference's uncertainty and corroboration requirements remain visible.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Omitting the inferential origin made the candidate identity appear more authoritatively grounded within the warrant pathway than the facial-recognition lead alone could support.

The affidavit reportedly replaced the actual facial-recognition origin with a generic 'credible source' description, materially changing the represented source role of the identity evidence within the warrant pathway.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: Associated Press occurrence reporting supports assessed physical-health, psychological, rights/liberty and financial/economic consequences. Six days of detention and continuing psychological distress remain the S3 controlling dimensions. Temporary illness and bounded economic disruption are assessed at S2 and do not raise the overall result; the later settlement is remediation and is not counted as harm magnitude.

dimensions.assessment_basis: Reid told AP that jail food made him sick during the six-day detention. No professional treatment, lasting illness or greater physical injury is reported, supporting temporary minor symptoms only.

Nearly a year after the arrest, Reid told AP that the experience still haunted him and that seeing police in his rear-view mirror triggered memories of what could have happened. This is meaningful sustained distress, bounded to one person and not shown to be grave, clinically treated or permanently impairing.
